_meta.status: FROZEN at D-76 before any physical tasting of Sessions 2-5. The founder may amend a session's gates only BEFORE that session's first tasting, as a new decision; never after tasting.
_meta.scale: 1-5 panel mean per gate; 'photo_ids' and 'panel_n' required with every score; a small directional R&D panel (n<8) reports raw values.
_meta.thresholds_label: NASHA R&D THRESHOLDS: NOT INDUSTRY STANDARDS. 1-5 scale. A construction passes an iteration only if EVERY gate is met at its stated time and no failure gate fires; two passing iterations before any winner; NONE WINS is valid.
_meta.d54: No beef, no pork, no hidden derivatives (lard in tortillas, stocks/bouillon/gelatin, animal rennet from a bovine source, Worcestershire, processing aids). No halal claim.
_meta.mustard_oil: EXCLUDED from all baselines (ledger V-72: FDA Import Alert 26-04 reportedly treats expressed mustard oil as an unsafe food additive (T1: search snippet only, the primary page was not read; it may also reach products labelled 'external use'). Excluded as a precaution; regulatory review pending, no legal conclusion). Use a neutral oil. Flag for regulatory review; never improvise a legal conclusion.

paneer-tikka-taco.question: Can recognizable paneer tikka and a credible Mexican taco become one coherent NASHA dish without either side disappearing, and which AVAILABLE heat source preserves the tikka identity well enough for early testing?

constructions.C: Tandoor (ONLY if a real appropriate tandoor is available; otherwise skip, do not simulate)

controls: Control: unmarinated paneer charred on the A heat source (shows what the marinade adds)
controlled: same paneer block and cut
same marinade batch and time
same corn tortilla batch, warmed the same way
same salsa, onion, cilantro, lime
same plate; 2 small tacos per plate
paneer-tikka-taco.test_variable: heat source (A vs B, C if available). A substitute is NOT the same as a tandoor; record the limitation.
paneer-tikka-taco.hypothesis: ANALYSIS, not evidence: very high direct heat for a short time gives char without drying the paneer; the marinade must be thick (hung curd) to cling; the tortilla and fresh salsa carry the Mexican identity; the dish is a taco if it is small, folded and eaten by hand, not a wrap.

constructions.A: Roast-first (blanch, steam-dry, thin yogurt-besan film, hot roast, glaze to order)
constructions.B: Batter-fried (thin rice-flour/cornflour batter, fry, glaze to order)

same corn tortilla batch
same plate; 2 small tacos per plate

gobi-taco.hypothesis: ANALYSIS, not evidence: roast-first keeps visible floret structure and avoids a fried-chicken look; batter-fry gives a stronger gobi-65 read and crunch but risks nugget look and fast softening under glaze. Fryer pressure is a real operational difference but culinary quality ranks first.

goat-birria.question: Does a NASHA adaptation (Indian technique layer) make Jalisco-style goat birria better than the plain Mexican adobo control while keeping the Mexican reference legible and the goat identity clear?

constructions.A: CONTROL: plain Mexican guajillo-ancho adobo, braised (no Indian layer)
constructions.B: A + technique layer only: whole spices dry-toasted and the adobo paste bhuna-fried until the oil separates; sealed pot
constructions.C: A + yogurt-papaya pre-marinade (tenderiser/flavour test); no other change

controls: The plain adobo (A) is the control: do NOT make it 'more Indian'. B and C must earn their place against A.
controlled: same goat cut, trim and weight per arm
ALL arms sealed identically (same lidded pot type; foil or dough seal) and braised at the same oven temperature
same chile lot, same vinegar
same stock (unsalted chicken or vegetable; no bouillon) and at least 500 ml braising liquid per pot
same corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime, salsa
same consomme cup and 30 ml tasting portion
tasted from blind codes with the control NOT identified to the panel
goat-birria.test_variable: adaptation layer (A control vs B technique vs C yogurt-papaya). Curry-leaf tadka is NOT in the first round (UNCERTAIN/ADVISOR).
goat-birria.hypothesis: ANALYSIS, not evidence: bone-in shoulder braised low and slow gives tender fibrous goat and a drinkable consomme; bhuna-frying the paste may add depth; yogurt-papaya may tenderise but risks a curry-like or lactic note. The Mexican reference (adobo, vinegar, consomme, onion, cilantro, lime) must stay legible; no cheese; no cheese-pull imagery.

gate_notes.improves_over_control: blind codes; B and C only (A, the control, is exempt); 1=worse, 3=same, 5=clearly better than the plain adobo (the control is not identified to the panel)
gate_notes.goat_identity: reads as goat, not beef quesabirria or lamb
gate_notes.service_practicality: cook judges batch, cooling, reheating and hold feasibility from measured data
gate_notes.taco_hold: clock starts when the plate goes down

failure_gates.GENERIC_QUESABIRRIA: reads as beef-style quesabirria (cheese pull, uniform red shredded meat)
failure_gates.POOR_YIELD: cooked yield or trim waste makes the batch impractical (measured, then judged)
failure_gates.D54: beef/pork in stock or bones, lard in tortillas

goat-birria.quantity_audit: 3 arms x 600 g bone-in = 1.8 kg cooks to about 300 g meat per arm, which is thin: buy 3.0 kg (800 g bone-in per arm plus a trial margin). Tortillas 3 arms x 2 tacos x 4 tasters + spare = 28. Stock/liquid 1.8 L. Dried chiles: about 50 g guajillo + 35 g ancho per arm = buy 150 g + 100 g. Yield, trim and consomme volume are MEASURED, not assumed.
day_plan: DAY 0 (sourcing): confirm goat cut/source and a food-safety plan; no purchase without a recorded source
DAY 1 AM: weigh goat (as bought), trim, weigh trim; arm C marinade 2 h at 5 C or below; toast/soak chiles, build adobo(s)
DAY 1: sear, braise A/B/C sealed in the oven (log time and temperature, test tenderness with a probe), rest

DAY 1 evening: cool IMMEDIATELY in shallow pans (no deep pots); log core temperature at 0, 30, 60, 120 min, then 4 h and 6 h; refrigerate. Until a food-safety professional confirms limits, do not eat goat that cooled slowly; when unsure, discard; never taste-test leftovers
DAY 2: skim the fat COLD (weigh), reheat to 74 C (165 F) within 2 hours, hold at 57 C (135 F) or above, dip tortillas in the surface fat and griddle to order
Plate within 3 min, score at T+0 and T+10 (clock starts when the plate goes down); photos; log reheat and hold at 60 and 120 min
safety: US FDA Food Code general values (T4 from general knowledge, NOT verified for Austin; local rules govern; a food-safety professional or the health department must confirm): cool from 57 C (135 F) to 21 C (70 F) within 2 h and to 5 C (41 F) within 4 more hours; reheat to 74 C (165 F) within 2 h; hold hot at 57 C (135 F) or above. Use shallow pans; never cool a big pot in the fridge.
If any cooling or reheating limit is missed the batch is UNSAFE: record and do not taste.
goat: strictly goat (D-54); not halal-claimed; ask the butcher about shared boards with beef/pork.
GAMY: record a 1-5 gaminess score per sample; the failure fires if the panel mean is 4.0 or higher.
goat-birria.panel: Minimum 4 tasters, at least 3 of whom did not cook; same tasting order for everyone, plain unsalted tortilla/cracker and room-temperature water between samples; blind codes from `python3 tools/t1_randomize.py <run>` plated by a second person (not double-blind). n<8: raw values only.
goat-birria.verify_labels: Read every jar, can, paste and packet label for animal ingredients (D-54) before cooking.
